title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: APPLICATION OF RADIATION TECHNOLOGIES FOR AGRICULTURE AND FOOD SECURITY
body_text:
Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC), a constituent unit of Department of Atomic Energy (DAE), has developed 72 improved varieties in different crops using radiation-induced mutagenesis along with cross breeding. These varieties have been released and notified for commercial cultivation across the country in collaboration with Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) and State Agricultural Universities (SAUs). These include 17 varieties in groundnut, 10 varieties in rice, 9 varieties each in mungbean and mustard, 8 varieties in urdbean, 5 varieties in pigeonpea, 3 varieties in sorghum, 2 varieties each in cowpea, wheat and soybean, one variety each in banana, sesame, linseed, sunflower and jute. Some of the desirable traits in these crops include higher yield, seed size, early maturity, climate resilient traits like drought, heat, salinity tolerance and resistance to diseases. Several of these varieties have high patronage from the farming community and are extensively grown in the country.
Genetic modifications induced through radiations in the different crops do not cause adverse effects. Prior to release, the developed varieties are thoroughly tested through multi-location evaluations over the years and released for commercial cultivation after attaining the superiority over the existing cultivars.
DAE has undertaken various initiatives to promote the adoption of improved crop varieties in the Indian farming communities. The steps include, large-scale quality seed production of Trombay varieties along with several state agricultural universities (SAUs) and supply to
State seed corporation,
ii. State agricultural departments,
National Institutes, State agricultural Universities,
v. Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs),
Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs),
vii. Farmer cooperatives,
Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs), Seed companies and
x. Farmers in several States
In addition, DAE has participated in Kisan Melas, Field days, provided technical guidance and training on cultivation practices, conducted exhibitions in different states in collaboration with SAUs. DAE has also conducted Outreach programmes, field demonstrations, distributed seed minikits of the improved Trombay varieties and conducted Public Awareness Programmes on Peaceful Uses of Atomic Energy to render benefit to hundreds of farmers.
DAE has developed radiation-based food preservation and food processing technologies to reduce the post harvesting losses and extend shelf life of agri products. Also, radiation-based protocols have also been developed for various agricultural products like vegetables, fruits, pulses, spices etc. The technology has been transferred to private entrepreneurs on non-exclusive basis, for commercialization and can be implemented through licensees.
Further, Government has implemented policy measures to expand the radiation technology for food preservation at the country level. Government of India has announced incentives for setting up of multiproduct food irradiation units under ‘Integrated Cold Chain & Value Addition Infrastructure’ of the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Sampada Yojana (PMKSY) scheme across the Nation in 2024-25. This scheme is open for application by the interested stakeholders.
In the state of Uttar Pradesh, three food irradiation facilities have been commissioned till date in the private sector.
In agriculture, DAE has been consistently evaluating their developed breeding lines/mutants in different crops and their release in different agro-climatic zones in respective states in collaboration with State Agricultural Universities (SAU) and various ICAR institutes. DAE has research collaborations and Memorandum of Understandings (MoUs) with the State Agricultural Universities in Assam, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Jammu and Kashmir, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal and following ICAR institutes:
ICAR - Indian Institute of Groundnut Research, Junagadh ICAR-National Soybean Research Institute, Indore ICAR-Indian Institute of Rapeseed Mustard Research, Bharatpur ICAR-Indian Institute of Oilseeds Research, Hyderabad ICAR-Indian Institute of Pulses Research, Kanpur and ICAR-National Research Centre for Banana, Trichy.
Department also funds several research projects on mutation breeding and food preservation through Board of Research in Nuclear Sciences (BRNS) projects, an Advisory Body of DAE.
This information was given by Union Minister of State for Prime Minister’s office and Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, in a written reply in the Lok Sabha today.

enrichment.summary: In a written Lok Sabha reply, Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh stated that BARC (under the Department of Atomic Energy) has developed 72 improved crop varieties through radiation-induced mutagenesis and cross-breeding, notified for commercial cultivation in collaboration with ICAR and State Agricultural Universities. These include varieties in groundnut, rice, mungbean, mustard, urdbean, pigeonpea and other crops with traits like higher yield, early maturity and climate resilience. DAE also promotes seed distribution, farmer outreach, and radiation-based food preservation technologies, with incentives for food irradiation units under PMKSY, including three such facilities commissioned in Uttar Pradesh.
enrichment.context: India's nuclear agriculture programme, run through BARC's Nuclear Agriculture and Biotechnology Division based at Trombay, is one of the lesser-known peaceful applications of atomic energy, distinct from power generation. Radiation-induced mutation breeding uses gamma rays or other radiation to induce genetic variability in crop seeds, which breeders then select for desirable traits like disease resistance, drought tolerance or higher yield—this is different from genetic engineering/GM technology since it does not involve inserting foreign genes, and mutant varieties are treated on par with conventionally bred varieties in regulatory terms. 'Trombay' varieties of groundnut, mustard, urdbean and others have found wide farmer adoption, especially in western and central India, contributing to food security and climate resilience in rainfed agriculture. The Bhabha Atomic Research Centre's involvement also extends to food irradiation for preservation—killing pathogens and extending shelf life of perishables—which supports post-harvest loss reduction, a persistent problem in Indian agriculture given inadequate cold-chain infrastructure. This links to the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Sampada Yojana (PMKSY), a food processing sector scheme aimed at modernizing infrastructure across the value chain, with a specific 2024-25 incentive to expand multiproduct food irradiation units, reflecting the government's food processing and value-addition push under 'Atmanirbhar Bharat' and doubling farmers' income goals.

prelims_questions.question: Radiation-induced mutation breeding, as practiced by BARC for developing improved crop varieties, primarily involves:
options: Insertion of foreign genes into the crop genome
Use of radiation to induce genetic variability followed by selection of desirable traits
Cloning of superior plant tissues in vitro
Cross-breeding of transgenic plants with wild relatives
prelims_questions.explanation: The release specifies that BARC develops improved crop varieties using 'radiation-induced mutagenesis along with cross breeding,' which induces genetic variation through radiation exposure, distinct from genetic engineering/GM technology.

prelims_questions.question: The Pradhan Mantri Kisan Sampada Yojana (PMKSY), mentioned in the context of incentives for food irradiation units, primarily aims to:
options: Provide direct income support to farmers
Modernize food processing and value-addition infrastructure including cold chains
Regulate minimum support prices for crops
prelims_questions.explanation: PMKSY is a food processing sector scheme; the release notes incentives for multiproduct food irradiation units under its 'Integrated Cold Chain & Value Addition Infrastructure' component.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the role of radiation technology in Indian agriculture, particularly in crop improvement through mutation breeding and in food preservation. How does this contribute to food security and reduction of post-harvest losses?
mains_questions.gs_paper: GS Paper 3 - Agriculture and Science & Technology

mains_questions.question: Examine the institutional collaboration model between the Department of Atomic Energy, ICAR, and State Agricultural Universities in developing and disseminating improved crop varieties. What lessons does this offer for inter-agency coordination in agricultural research and extension?
